approachQuestion.prompt:
Cables with no substitute. In an undirected network, return every cable whose removal would increase the number of connected components. Return each cable once as [minEndpoint,maxEndpoint], in any order. The graph may already be disconnected.

Input: read-only adjacency lists for IDs 0..V-1, 1 <= V <= 200000, 0 <= E <= 400000. The graph is simple: no self-loops or parallel edges. Every cable is listed at both endpoints. Output [] when no cable is critical.

Example: lists=[[1],[0,2,3],[1,3],[1,2],[]], output=[[0,1]]. The triangle on 1,2,3 provides substitutes for its three cables; vertex 4 is isolated.

options.text: Run a DFS forest with discovery times and low values. Skip only the parent edge. Fold an already discovered non-parent neighbor’s discovery time into low[u]; after finishing a DFS child v, fold low[v] into low[u]. Emit tree edge u-v exactly when low[v] > discovery[u].
options.feedback: The strict inequality means the child subtree has no edge back to u or an earlier ancestor, so removing its only tree connection separates that subtree. A return connection prevents that separation.

options.text: Use recursive DFS with the same discovery/low update rules and strict child test, scanning all components. Assume enough call-stack capacity for V frames.
options.feedback: Recursion implements the same postorder calculation. Including its call stack, it has the same time and auxiliary-space bounds as explicit resumable frames.

options.text: Run a DFS forest and emit every edge used to discover a new vertex.
options.feedback: A triangle has two DFS tree edges but no critical cable. Non-tree edges can provide an alternate route around a tree edge.

options.text: Use the discovery/low DFS rules but emit u-v whenever low[v] >= discovery[u].
options.feedback: In a triangle rooted at 0, a child subtree can return to 0, giving low[child]=discovery[0]. Removing the root-child edge still leaves an alternate triangle route. Equality does not make a cable critical.

feedback.reason: A critical edge requires the child subtree to have no return route even to its parent. This makes the comparison strict, unlike the related vertex-removal criterion.
details: Initialize discovery to unseen. For every unseen root, start DFS frames containing vertex, parent and next-neighbor index. On discovery, assign increasing discovery[u] and low[u]=discovery[u]. While scanning u, skip its parent; an unseen neighbor becomes a child frame, and a discovered non-parent neighbor updates low[u] with its discovery time. When child v finishes, update low[parent] from low[v] and append the normalized parent-v pair if low[v] > discovery[parent]. Finish every component.

A child edge is a bridge exactly when its subtree cannot reach the parent or an earlier ancestor: low[child]>discovery[parent]. Equality means an alternative route reaches the parent, so the strict comparison matters.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze dfs-lowlink-bridges exactly as revealed. V counts vertices and E undirected simple edges, stored twice. Preallocate V-entry discovery/low arrays and V fixed-size DFS frames; each frame resumes at its saved neighbor index. No recursion is used in this analyzed method. Use a result buffer for at most V-1 bridge pairs, returning only the filled portion without a second copy. Include result-writing time but exclude result storage. Constant-time indices, arithmetic and stack operations; no hashing, shifting, input copies or amortized growth. Include array initialization and root scanning.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(E(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Saved DFS frame positions inspect adjacency entries once and combine low values on return.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: saved frame indices inspect each of 2E adjacency entries once, each vertex is discovered/finished once, and at most V-1 critical pairs are written. Discovery, low and frames use O(V). The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” drops those structures. C repeatedly removes edges and searches again, which the revealed postorder calculation avoids. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” counts edge storage although the original lists are used without copying and returned pairs are excluded.
